newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says will work hard with partners.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says will work hard with partners.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday it acknowledged the 30-day deadline given it by the Indonesian government and will work hard with its partners to resolve all outstanding issues.

"During this period, we will work diligently with senior executives of our Indonesian partners, PT Askatindo Karya Minerals and PT Amsya Lyna to resolve outstanding matters," Bre-X chairman, president and chief executive David Walsh said in a statement.
The Indonesian government last week sent Bre-X and Barrick Gold Corp a letter instructing them to resolve all issues with Bre-X's Indonesian partners within 30 days.
The Indonesian government last November told Bre-X to forge an alliance with Barrick to develop the massive Busang deposit, which contains at least 57 million ounces of gold.
But the two companies have yet to announce a deal.
Since then, Placer Dome Inc publicly proposed a merger of Placer and Bre-X to develop Busang, with a 40 percent slice of the deposit going to Indonesian interests.

"Bre-X recognizes that the development of the Busang deposits is a matter of the highest priority for the government of Indonesia, and we are in complete agreement with the government on the need to move forward with the expeditious development of Busang in a manner that gives maximum consideration to the interests of the government and people of Indonesia," Walsh said.

"We remain anxious to join forces with local and foreign partners acceptable to the government of Indonesia, and we are looking forward to further discussions with the government representatives, our Indonesian partners and other interested parties to reconcile all remaining issues so work can begin on this vitally important development project," he added.
Walsh said Bre-X is optimistic that it will be granted the contract of work to allow it to develop the Busang gold deposit.
